turnaround_reason: A $10B-revenue customer-experience (BPO) outsourcer cut in half on the 'AI kills call centers' fear plus a heavy post-Webhelp debt load. Trades at ~2.3x forward earnings and 0.63x book as the market prices in secular decline; the turnaround bet is that AI becomes a bookings tailwind while FCF pays down debt.
bullish_points: Extreme cheapness: ~2.3x forward P/E, 0.63x book, 5.4x EV/EBITDA — deep-value optionality if revenue merely stabilizes.
Strong cash generation: record Q2 operating cash flow $258M, ~$242M adjusted FCF, $775M TTM FCF; management prioritizing debt reduction over buybacks.
AI narrative flipping from threat to tailwind: iX Suite deals +400% YoY, large jump in AI-related bookings, growing recurring 'Intelligent Experience' revenue.
Insider buying by CEO (Caldwell) and CFO (Valentine) at $21-28, near current levels — alignment at the lows.
bearish_points: Revenue growth is stuck near zero (FY26 guide cut to +0.25% to +1.25% constant-currency) — no top-line inflection yet.
Heavy leverage: $5.5B debt, debt-to-equity ~204x, EV ~$6.9B dwarfs the $1.7B market cap — equity is a thin sliver of the capital structure.
Negative TTM profit margin (-13%, likely goodwill/impairment) despite positive cash flow — GAAP optics remain ugly.
Large-holder overhang: Groupe Bruxelles Lambert dumped 6.0M shares (~$133M) in April — a big seller against the tape.
Core BPO is exactly the labor-arbitrage business most exposed to genuine agentic-AI disruption; the tailwind claim is unproven.
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings — evidence on whether AI bookings convert to revenue growth and whether debt paydown is visibly progressing.
suggested_trade: Spot only, small starter. Deep-value/value-trap coin flip; size for a full drawdown to the $19 low. Wait for Q3 revenue trend before adding.
key_risk: AI genuinely compresses BPO volumes and revenue turns negative while the debt load leaves no margin for error — the classic value trap.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows revenue turning negative, AI bookings failing to convert, or further large-holder selling; leverage leaves no room for an operational miss.
